purpose: DEV-ONLY visual-lab dataset. Not part of the production catalogue.

resources.name: Amber Nugget
resources.description: Fossilised tree resin: translucent gold, often cloudy, sometimes with trapped insects or plant fragments. Worked into beads and ornaments since the Upper Palaeolithic.
resources.period: Resin tens of millions of years old; worked since the Upper Palaeolithic

resources.name: Nephrite Jade Pebble
resources.description: Dense, very tough green stone often found as water-worn cobbles; ground into axes and ornaments in Neolithic China and elsewhere.
resources.period: Worked from the Neolithic (about 5000 BCE in China)

resources.name: Ivory Tusk
resources.description: Long curved tooth of elephant or mammoth showing fine concentric growth layers; carved since the Palaeolithic.
features: hollow root cavity at the base
concentric growth rings at the cut end

resources.name: Pearl Oyster
resources.description: Bivalve mollusc whose pearly nacre lines the shell; natural pearls were gathered as ornaments in many ancient cultures.
resources.period: Pearls used as ornament since antiquity

resources.name: Geode
resources.description: Hollow rock cavity lined with inward-pointing crystals, usually quartz, revealed when the rock is broken open.

resources.name: Coral Branch
resources.description: Branching calcium-carbonate skeleton of colonial marine polyps, long used for beads and charms.

resources.name: Bamboo Stalk
resources.description: Hollow, jointed grass stem with regular nodes and thin leaves; used for building, tools and containers across Asia.

resources.name: Petrified Wood
resources.description: Fossil wood whose cell structure was replaced by minerals, preserving bark texture and growth rings in stone.
features: concentric growth rings at the cut face

resources.name: Rock Salt Crystal
resources.description: Cubic crystals of halite mined from evaporite beds; mined and traded for seasoning and preserving food.

resources.name: Natural Sponge
resources.description: Porous fibrous skeleton of a marine sponge, full of open channels; used for washing and padding since antiquity.

resources.name: Boomerang
resources.description: Curved throwing stick with an aerofoil section; Aboriginal Australian examples include returning and non-returning hunting types.
resources.period: Known from at least about 10,000 years ago
features: two angled arms in a flat V

resources.name: Antler Billet
resources.description: Short length of antler used as a soft hammer to strike flakes from flint during knapping.
features: knobbed base where it was shed

resources.name: Fish Gorge
resources.description: Straight double-pointed sliver tied at the middle to a line; swallowed by the fish, it turns crosswise in the gut.

resources.name: Fire Plough
resources.description: A blunt stick rubbed along a groove in a softer board until friction dust glows into an ember.
features: short pushing stick at an angle
dust pile at the groove end

resources.name: Knobbed Wooden Club
resources.description: A heavy hardwood club with a thickened striking head and slim grip, used for hunting and fighting.

resources.name: Bone Comb
resources.description: Flat bar of bone or antler with fine teeth cut along one or both edges, often decorated.

resources.name: Shell Scoop
resources.description: A large bivalve shell used as a ladle or scraper, sometimes with a hole for a handle.

resources.name: Bone Whistle
resources.description: Hollow bird bone with a notch and finger hole that sounds a pitch when blown across; found in Upper Palaeolithic sites.

resources.name: Hand Drill (Friction Fire)
resources.description: A straight spindle spun between the palms against a hearth board to produce an ember.

resources.name: Frame Drum
resources.description: A shallow wooden hoop with a skin stretched over one side; among the oldest drum forms, shown in Mesopotamian art.

resources.name: Yarn Swift
resources.description: An adjustable skeleton drum that holds a skein open so the yarn can be wound off in an even run onto a ball or bobbin.

resources.name: Distaff
resources.description: A forked or caged staff that holds a mass of flax or wool for the spinner to draw from.
features: loose fibre bundle at the top

resources.name: Weaving Sword
resources.description: A long flat wooden or bone blade slipped between warp threads to open a shed and beat the weft tight.

resources.name: Spinning Wheel
resources.description: A hand- or foot-driven wheel that turns a spindle to spin fibre into thread; evidence from about the 11th to 13th centuries CE.

resources.name: Felt
resources.description: Dense non-woven textile made by matting wool with moisture, heat and pressure; long used in Central Asia for tents and rugs.

resources.name: Wicker Basket
resources.description: A container woven from flexible willow rods around upright stakes, with an arched handle.

resources.name: Bobbin Lace on a Pillow
resources.description: Lace plaited by crossing threads wound on weighted wooden bobbins, pinned over a pattern on a cushion.

resources.name: Knitting Needles
resources.description: A pair of long pointed rods forming loops of yarn into fabric; the oldest known knitted pieces come from Egypt around the 11th to 13th centuries CE.
features: loops of stitches on the needle

resources.name: Cotton Boll
resources.description: The seed pod of the cotton plant, splitting into a ball of white fibre; cotton cloth is known from the Indus Valley about the 3rd millennium BCE.
resources.period: Cloth from about the 3rd millennium BCE

resources.name: Silk Cocoon
resources.description: The oval cocoon of the silkworm, spun from one continuous thread that can be unwound for silk.
resources.period: Silk production in China dates from the Neolithic

resources.name: Ard Plough
resources.description: A simple wooden scratch plough drawn by oxen that cuts a furrow without turning the soil.

resources.name: Dasher Butter Churn
resources.description: An upright wooden barrel with a plunger (dasher) worked up and down to turn cream into butter.

resources.name: Chaff Sieve Tray
resources.description: A shallow woven tray tossed so the wind carries chaff from heavier grain.

resources.name: Dev Lab Shaduf
resources.description: A pivoted pole with a bucket at one end and a counterweight at the other, for lifting water from a river or canal.
resources.period: Mesopotamia and Egypt, from about 2000 BCE
features: two upright posts with a crossbar
counterweight lump at the other end

resources.name: Seed Drill
resources.description: A wheeled hopper that drops seed through tubes into furrows in rows; mechanical forms are recorded in China and later in Europe.
resources.period: Early forms in China; European designs from the 16th to 18th centuries

resources.name: Harrow
resources.description: A frame set with tines or spikes dragged over ploughed land to break clods and cover seed.

resources.name: Ox Yoke
resources.description: A shaped wooden beam across the necks of a pair of draught animals, held by bows, to share a load.

resources.name: Skep Beehive
resources.description: A dome-shaped hive coiled from straw, once standard across Europe for keeping honeybees.

resources.name: Pitchfork
resources.description: A long-handled fork with two or three tines for lifting hay and straw.

resources.name: Grain Scoop
resources.description: A wide shovel-shaped wooden scoop used to lift and toss threshed grain on the floor or into storage.

resources.name: Amphora
resources.description: A narrow-necked, two-handled clay jar with a pointed foot, used to ship wine, oil and fish sauce around the Mediterranean.
resources.period: Bronze Age to the Roman period
features: two looped handles at the neck

resources.name: Potter's Wheel
resources.description: A rotating disc on which clay is shaped; the fast wheel appears in Mesopotamia from about 3500 BCE.
features: clay form being shaped on top

resources.name: Clay Oil Lamp
resources.description: A small closed bowl with a filling hole and a nozzle for a wick, burning olive oil.
resources.period: Bronze Age to the Roman period and later

resources.name: Stained Glass Rose Window
resources.description: A circular Gothic window of radiating stone tracery filled with coloured glass panes.
resources.period: Gothic cathedrals of the 12th and 13th centuries
features: small trefoil openings around the rim

resources.name: Glassblowing Pipe
resources.description: A long hollow iron tube used to gather molten glass on its end and inflate it into a bubble.
resources.period: Invented about the 1st century BCE in the eastern Mediterranean

resources.name: Framed Sandglass
resources.description: Two glass bulbs joined by a narrow neck through which sand flows to measure a fixed time.
features: top and bottom caps with posts

resources.name: Porcelain Vase
resources.description: A tall vase of white, translucent kaolin ceramic painted with blue underglaze; true porcelain developed in China around the 7th to 10th centuries CE.
resources.period: From about the 7th to 10th century CE; blue-and-white from the 14th century

resources.name: Terracotta Figurine
resources.description: A small hand-modelled figure of fired clay; some of the oldest known ceramics are figurines from about 29,000 to 25,000 years ago.

resources.name: Kylix
resources.description: A wide, shallow, stemmed Greek drinking cup with two horizontal handles, painted inside with a round scene.

resources.name: Roman Glass Flask
resources.description: A blown glass bottle with a rounded body and a long thin neck, used for oils and perfumes.

resources.name: Anvil
resources.description: A heavy block with a flat face, a tapered horn and a square hole for tools, on which hot metal is hammered.
resources.period: Iron Age onward; stone anvils earlier

resources.name: Crucible
resources.description: A small heat-proof clay vessel with a pouring lip for melting metals.

resources.name: Blacksmith Tongs
resources.description: Two long pivoted arms ending in jaws that grip hot metal at the forge.

resources.name: Forge Bellows
resources.description: A folding leather-and-wood chamber that blasts air through a nozzle to heat a fire.
resources.period: Used since at least the Bronze Age

resources.name: Bronze Sword
resources.description: A leaf-shaped cast bronze blade with a midrib and riveted hilt, widespread in Bronze Age Europe.

resources.name: Bronze Mirror
resources.description: A polished bronze disc with a handle and an engraved back, used from Egypt to China.

resources.name: Horseshoe
resources.description: A U-shaped iron plate nailed to a horse's hoof; nailed iron shoes are widespread in medieval Europe.

resources.name: Bronze Bell
resources.description: A cup-shaped cast bronze bell with a clapper; Chinese bronze bells date to the Shang period.

resources.name: Cast Cauldron
resources.description: A round-bellied pot with ring handles and sometimes three legs, hung or set over a fire.

resources.name: Corinthian Helmet
resources.description: A bronze Greek helmet covering the whole head with slits for the eyes and a nose guard.

resources.name: Roman Arch
resources.description: A semicircular arch of wedge-shaped stones around a central keystone, carrying loads by compression.
resources.period: Roman, from about the 2nd century BCE

resources.name: Roman Aqueduct
resources.description: A multi-tier arched bridge carrying a water channel across a valley, as at the Pont du Gard.

resources.name: Ziggurat
resources.description: A stepped mud-brick temple tower rising in tiers, with ramps and a shrine on top.

resources.name: Step Pyramid
resources.description: A stack of mastaba-like stone tiers, as in the pyramid of Djoser at Saqqara.

resources.name: Obelisk
resources.description: A tall four-sided tapering monolith with a small pyramid-shaped tip.

resources.name: Trilithon
resources.description: Two upright stones capped by a lintel, as in the sarsen circle at Stonehenge.

resources.name: Lighthouse
resources.description: A tall tapered tower with a lantern room at the top; the Pharos of Alexandria was built in the 3rd century BCE.

resources.name: Pagoda
resources.description: A multi-tiered tower with projecting upturned eaves on each storey, found across East Asia.
resources.period: East Asia, from the 1st millennium CE

resources.name: Flying Buttress
resources.description: An arched half-bridge outside a Gothic wall that transmits roof thrust to a heavy pier.

resources.name: Suspension Bridge
resources.description: A roadway hung from vertical cables that hang from main cables draped over towers.

resources.name: Post Windmill
resources.description: A wooden mill body with four sails that pivots on a central post so it can face the wind.

resources.name: Stream Paddle Wheel
resources.description: A vertical wheel with flat paddles dipped into a flowing stream so the current turns it.
resources.period: Greco-Roman, by about the 1st century BCE

resources.name: Dev Lab Archimedes Screw
resources.description: A helical blade inside a tilted cylinder; turning it lifts water up the slope.

resources.name: Trebuchet
resources.description: A siege engine using a pivoting beam, a counterweight and a sling to hurl stones.

resources.name: Treadwheel Crane
resources.description: A large wheel walked from inside that winds a rope over a jib to lift stone blocks.

resources.name: Crankshaft
resources.description: A shaft with offset throws that turns back-and-forth motion into rotation; crank-and-rod machines are known from the 3rd century CE.
resources.period: From late antiquity; engine use from the 19th century

resources.name: Dev Lab Cam and Follower
resources.description: A profiled rotating disc that pushes a rod up and down; used in medieval water-powered stamping mills.

resources.name: Dev Lab Anchor Escapement
resources.description: Anchor-shaped pallets rocking against a toothed escape wheel to meter a clock's drive; late 17th century.

resources.name: Piston Pump
resources.description: A cylinder with a plunger and one-way valves that lifts water; Ctesibius of Alexandria described such pumps in the 3rd century BCE.

resources.name: Dev Lab Flywheel
resources.description: A heavy wheel with a thick rim that stores rotational energy to smooth a machine's motion.

resources.name: Astrolabe
resources.description: A disc instrument with a rotating star map over engraved plates and a sighting arm, used to find time and star positions.
resources.period: Hellenistic, refined in the medieval Islamic world

resources.name: Sundial
resources.description: A flat plate with radiating hour lines and an angled gnomon whose shadow indicates the time.

resources.name: Sextant
resources.description: A sixth-of-a-circle arc with an index arm, mirrors and a small telescope for measuring star elevation.

resources.name: Dev Lab Aneroid Dial
resources.description: A round dial that shows air pressure through a flexing sealed metal capsule; invented in 1844.

resources.name: Mercury Thermometer
resources.description: A glass tube with a bulb of mercury that rises along a scale; Fahrenheit made precise ones in 1714.

resources.name: Brass Tube Microscope
resources.description: A tube with an eyepiece and objective lens over a stage, first built in the Netherlands in the late 16th century.

resources.name: Dev Lab Sliding Scale Rule
resources.description: A ruler with a sliding strip carrying logarithmic scales for multiplying and dividing, devised by William Oughtred in 1622.

resources.name: Abacus
resources.description: A frame with rods or wires of sliding beads for counting, used in many ancient cultures.

resources.name: Armillary Sphere
resources.description: Nested metal rings representing celestial circles around a central globe; used in Greek and Chinese astronomy.
resources.period: Greek 3rd century BCE; Chinese Han dynasty

resources.name: Glass Prism
resources.description: A triangular glass block that spreads white light into a rainbow; studied by Isaac Newton in the 1660s.

resources.name: Solar Panel
resources.description: A tilted grid of silicon photovoltaic cells in an aluminium frame; the silicon solar cell dates from 1954.

resources.name: Wind Turbine
resources.description: A tall tower topped by a nacelle and a three-blade rotor that turns wind into electricity.
resources.period: Electric turbines from the 1880s; modern designs from the 1980s

resources.name: Printed Circuit Board
resources.description: A flat board with etched copper traces linking components; PCB methods developed in the 1930s and 1940s.

resources.name: Spinning Disk Storage Unit
resources.description: Stacked magnetic platters spun under a swinging actuator arm; the first was IBM's RAMAC in 1956.

resources.name: Satellite Dish
resources.description: A parabolic reflector that focuses microwave signals onto a feed horn on an arm.

resources.name: Lithium-ion Cell
resources.description: A cylindrical metal can enclosing a spiral-wound electrode sandwich; first commercialised in 1991.

resources.name: Optical Fibre Cable
resources.description: A glass core and cladding with protective layers that guides light for data; practical low-loss fibre dates from 1970.

resources.name: LED Bulb
resources.description: A screw-base lamp with a finned heat sink and a diffuser dome over an array of light-emitting diodes.

resources.name: Quadcopter Drone
resources.description: A small aircraft with four rotors on arms around a central body; consumer models spread in the 2010s.

resources.name: Turbofan Jet Engine
resources.description: A gas-turbine engine with a large front fan, compressor and turbine stages, used on modern airliners.
resources.period: Jet engines from the 1930s and 1940s; turbofans from the 1960s
